content: This is interesting, as I had never investigated this. When entering email address on the TO line, Thunderbird does a simple search, character by characters as the letters are entered. For example, had you entered 'office' the default would have been listed first. The only place to my knowledge where the default setting is effective is if you set the addressbook to list on left side of compose screen ( done by pressing F9). Then, if you use the addressbook list and click an entry, the default appears on the TO line. Since the search for the TO line is character by character, identifying by default is not possible. My suggestion is to use the F9 list when wanting to send by default, and use the addressbook, locating name and then selecting the desired alternate email address.

content:
It looks to me like a program called "IObit" has automatically updated Thunderbird, that is, Thunderbird did not update itself. First thing to do is TURN THAT FEATURE OFF! It's dangerous, as you have discovered.

After doing that, I think your best bet is to make a safety copy of your entire Thunderbird Profile, which is the folder, separate from the programs itself, that contains all your email accounts, messages, folders, passwords, preferences, everything. Put the copy in a safe, convenient place on your computer. The default location of the folder to back up is:

C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird

Then, uninstall whatever remnants are left of the program, if possible, then reinstall Thunderbird using the installer from the official source

https://www.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/all/

if you're lucky it will detect your existing profile and you'll be back in business. If not, there are ways to import the old profile if it is still intact.
